cases.why: a fault in the second of three statements undoes the first write (the issue's Set(a, 1) then Set(b, 100 / m))
a fault in the last statement undoes the two writes before it
a fault in the first statement has nothing to undo
a type error is a fault too (replay: replay-type-error; the page's s - 1 is NaN, so replay-non-finite) and undoes the write before it
the undo restores what the field held before the handler, not its initial value
a later event runs on the committed state: after the fault, fixing m lets the same event complete
a fault after an await undoes the writes since the await and keeps the ones before it, which were painted when the handler suspended (the write of the awaiting statement itself is committed too)
an event that runs while the handler is suspended is not undone by the later fault (no stale snapshot is put back)
the same handler completes when nothing faults
a superseded await is not a fault: the writes before both awaits stay, only the newer continuation runs
a failed net.get is an Err value, not a fault: the handler runs to the end
the result of the awaiting statement is committed and shown: a fault after it undoes the later writes, keeps the result, and the view is redrawn to show it
